A slow origin

From a workshop in Portland.

I started in a tiny Tuesday in a leaky garage off Alberta Street. Two woodworkers, one welder, and a small kiln. We wanted a kettle that respected the ritual — heavy enough to hold its line, quiet enough to start the day with. So we made one. Then we made it again, and again, until the spout poured the way we wanted it to.

Each Northwind is hand-finished and tested with water before it leaves. We don't ship on Mondays. We sit the kettle on the sill, watch the morning, and decide if it deserves the name.

— Tomás & June, founders

Questions, answered

Before you brew.

Is the kettle safe on induction stovetops?

Yes — the base is a tri-clad ferromagnetic build that's rated for induction, gas, electric, and ceramic. We recommend against flame stoves over high heat.

How long does it take to boil 600 ml?

About 4 minutes on induction, 5 minutes on gas. The triple-clad base is built to hold its heat — a little slower than thin kettles, but it loses less between pours.

Can the walnut handle go in the dishwasher?

No — please. The walnut is finished with food-safe oil and will dry out in a dishwasher. Hand-wash with mild soap and re-oil every few months with our walnut handle care kit.

Do you ship internationally?

We ship to the US, Canada, the UK, the EU, and Japan. Orders above $80 ship free domestically. International rates calculate at checkout.

What is the lifetime craft warranty?

If anything fails because of how we made it, we'll fix it or replace it — for the life of the kettle. Wear from use is welcome and considered part of how it gets to know your kitchen.
